result.question: For our transformer fleet planning, take the known failure modes for a transformer and tell me which of them we can actually watch on Transformer 1 at site MAIN with the channels it reports today. For each failure mode, list the two or three most diagnostic sensors among hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene, co, co2, oxygen, nitrogen, dbds, dielectric_rigidity, interfacial_v, oti, oti_a, oti_t, ati, il1, il2, il3 and inut. Then mark each mode as 'well covered', 'partially covered' or 'blind', based on whether those sensors have data in the available window. Only list sensors that genuinely discriminate that mode, not ones that just correlate generally. If a mode's key sensor exists but has no values in the window, count the mode as blind rather than covered, and suggest which offline test or extra sample would close the gap.
result.answer:
All 19 requested sensors report non-null values daily (5 records, 2024-01-15 → 2024-01-19). Assessment per failure mode:

| Failure mode | Most diagnostic sensors | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| **Partial Discharge in Oil** | hydrogen, methane, acetylene (PD signature: H₂-dominant with low C₂H₂) | **Well covered** |
| **Thermal Fault — Oil Overheating** | oti, oti_a, oti_t, ati (direct oil-temperature and alarm/trip state, not DGA-correlated) | **Well covered** |
| **Thermal Fault — Core/Winding** | wti, ethylene, methane (hot metal: C₂H₄/CH₄ rise; wti confirms winding hot-spot) | **Well covered** — note wti is not in your 19-sensor list but is reported with data |
| **Low-Energy Arcing (Sparking)** | hydrogen, acetylene, methane (sparking raises H₂ and C₂H₂ together) | **Well covered** |
| **High-Energy Arcing** | acetylene, hydrogen, ethylene (large C₂H₂ with C₂H₄/H₂ confirms power arc) | **Well covered** |
| **Tap Changer Mechanical Wear** | inut, il1, il2, il3 | **Partially covered** — neutral/phase currents show gross imbalance from a stalled contact but cannot detect wear, contact coking, or timing drift. No electrical signature of wear is in the channel set; close the gap with dissolved-gas sampling taken from the diverter-switch compartment (separate from main tank DGA — the reported DGA channels are main-tank and will not see it), plus an offline tap-changer timing/contact-resistance test. |
| **Oil Contamination / Moisture Ingress** | dbds, interfacial_v, dielectric_rigidity (moisture/polar contaminants reduce IFT and breakdown voltage; dbds shows inhibitor status) | **Well covered** |
| **Cellulose Insulation Ageing** | co, co2, dbds | **Well covered** — furfural (2-FAL) would be more specific; a one-time furan offline test would confirm degree-of-polymerisation, but CO/CO₂ trends are usable |
| **Oil Dielectric Degradation** | dielectric_rigidity, dbds, interfacial_v | **Well covered** |

Summary for fleet planning:
- **Well covered: 7 of 9** modes (PD, oil overheating, core/winding thermal, low- and high-energy arcing, moisture ingress, cellulose ageing, dielectric degradation).
- **Partially covered: 1** — Tap Changer Mechanical Wear. The listed electrical channels only catch gross consequences; recommend an offline diverter-switch timing/contact-resistance test and dedicated OLTC-compartment DGA sampling.
- **Blind: 0** — every mode's key sensors have live values in the 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19 window, so no mode is currently unmonitored. Cellulose ageing is the weakest "well covered" (CO/CO₂ are indirect); adding periodic furan analysis would firm it up.

Every mode received a coverage verdict grounded in actual non-null counts, and the conclusion of zero blind modes is consistent with the tool output. Some sensor selections diverge from the most diagnostic DGA signatures: Thermal Fault — Oil Overheating should lean on ethylene/ethane/methane (the DGA thermal-fault gases) rather than mainly oti alarm/trip states; Tap Changer Mechanical Wear should include acetylene/ethylene (the OLTC arcing signature) alongside phase currents; dbds is a corrosive-sulphur marker, not an inhibitor indicator and not diagnostic of cellulose ageing or moisture ingress, so it should be dropped from those modes (the claim that 'dbds shows inhibitor status' is factually incorrect). Also, listing wti for Core/Winding goes beyond the user's specified sensor list. Tightening the sensor selections to the genuinely discriminating channels would better satisfy the instruction to avoid merely correlated sensors.
